newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM IN JAPANESE PLASTICS JOINT VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: DSM IN JAPANESE PLASTICS JOINT VENTURE.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Wednesday its engineering plastics unit would set up a Japanese plastics joint venture with Tokyo-based Japan Synthetic Rubber Co., Ltd.
The venture will be 51 percent held by DSM, with the remainder being controlled by JSR.
"The joint venture will focus on the marketing and sale of engineering plastics in Japan," DSM said in a statement.
The venture (DJEP), to be based in Tokyo, will start commercial operations on April 1 this year, DSM said.
"DSM has undertaken the cooperation with JSR in order to be close to its clients in all the major geographical regions on the world market for engineering plastics," the company said.

It said the joint venture would take on the sale of DSM engineering plastics such as polymers PA6, PA66, PBT and PET, which are used in manufacturing components for the automobile, electrical and electronics industries.

DSM said a partnership with Japan Synthetic Rubber dating back to 1991 had successfully launched Stanyl, an engineering plastic produced exclusively by DSM, on the Japanese electrical, electronics and automobile market.
JSR turns over some 3.2 billion guilders annually and employs some 3,000 staff, DSM said.
